title: What If Space Debris Made Orbit Unusable?

scenes.text: What if one crash made orbit unusable? It has a name: Kessler syndrome.
Tens of thousands of large objects are tracked in orbit, with hundreds of thousands of smaller pieces flying alongside them.
A piece of debris just one centimeter wide travels at around seven to eight kilometers per second. That's enough to wreck a satellite.
In 1978, scientists Donald Kessler and Burton Cour-Palais warned that crashes create debris that causes more crashes.
Fragments would be added faster than the atmosphere can pull them down, so the cloud keeps growing.
Some orbits could become too dangerous to use. The satellites we depend on for navigation and weather couldn't safely stay there.
